textbookBox.concept: The chapter asks you to listen quietly to the sounds around you and think whether things around you listen to you too. Then it introduces Jahnavi, a bright girl in a coastal village in India.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: The chapter asks you to listen quietly to the sounds around you and think whether things around you listen to you too. Then it introduces Jahnavi, a bright girl in a coastal village in India.
beats.speakEn: The chapter asks you to listen quietly to the sounds around you and think whether things around you listen to you too. Then it introduces Jahnavi, a bright girl in a coastal village in India.

beats.en: Jahnavi is crying by the river when a kingfisher, a green lizard and a bamboo thicket are all around her. Suddenly a sleepy, murmuring voice asks what is the matter. She is startled, because she thought she was alone.

textbookBox.concept: Jahnavi says even little Ramu goes to school. The River says it is a pity the school is not by the sea, because it could carry her, though she would get her feet wet.

beats.en: Jahnavi says even little Ramu goes to school. The River says it is a pity the school is not by the sea, because it could carry her, though she would get her feet wet.
beats.speakEn: Jahnavi says even little Ramu goes to school. The River says it is a pity the school is not by the sea, because it could carry her, though she would get her feet wet.

beats.en: The next day Jahnavi gathers courage and reaches the school, breathless. She stands by the door while the teacher reads a story about a prince called Ashoka who became a great king.
